title: What If Every Peatland Dried Out? Their Carbon Outweighs Forests

scenes.text: What if every peatland dried out? They cover three percent of land and outweigh every forest.
Peatlands cover about three percent of Earth's land, yet store roughly twice as much carbon as all the world's forests.
That carbon built up slowly, from plant layers that stayed waterlogged and barely rotted, often over thousands of years.
Drain or burn a peatland, and it flips from absorbing carbon to releasing centuries of it.
About 15 percent of peatlands are already drained, and their CO2 equals about 10 percent of annual fossil fuel emissions.
Dry out the rest, and the largest carbon vault on land becomes a source. Thousands of years of storage, undone.
